propositions: Changing a ticket's type silently replays a plan-review verdict computed under different criteria, because reuse paths do not compare type against the stored sidecar value.

Type affects plan-review scoring in four locations: bug_tier assignment, exemptions for bug/session_log/code_review/identity, and distinct bug branch logic, so a plan certified as bug (exempt) incorrectly passes when retyped to task (non-exempt).
The material_fingerprint hashes ticket_id, description, file_impact, children, and conditionally file_impact_scope, but omits ticket_type, so type changes do not invalidate the fingerprint basis.

Both idempotent_reuse and verdict_reuse must read the stored ticket_type from the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar and return None when it differs from the current context type, failing open when the stored type is absent or empty.
End-to-end: a scratch ticket certified as bug then retyped to task must report runner=pydantic_ai (not reused) on the next review-plan, proving the stale verdict is rejected.
